claims.text: A machine-learning potential can substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion properties for high-entropy systems.
A machine-learning potential can substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
A machine-learning potential can maintain accurate predictions for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method applies faithfully to both solid and fluid states.
Local lattice distortion is a structural mediator relevant to the proposed machine-learning method.
Chemical clustering is a structural mediator relevant to the proposed machine-learning method.
A machine-learning potential learns from existing data.
A machine-learning potential can make predictions for new alloy systems.
Using a machine-learning potential reduces the need for expensive and time-consuming simulations.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will improve accuracy relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
High-entropy alloys are systems containing multiple principal elements.
The proposed method is applicable to high-entropy systems at temperatures of at least 1000 K.

A conventional interatomic potential can quantitatively reproduce selected structural properties, relative stability, pair probabilities, and high-temperature short-range ordering in quinary Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni when compared with first-principles calculations and experiments.
